source.title: Double Descent and Other Interpolation Phenomena in GANs
source.authors: L. Luzi; Yehuda Dar; Richard Baraniuk

page_placements.theme: Supervision and optimization can induce generative-model double descent

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own results showing that the double-descent pattern depends on the GAN training objective: it is absent for metric- or f-divergence-trained interpolating generators, while purpose-built pseudo-supervision can produce double or triple descent.
record.gate_note: The paper's own GAN and PCA experiments are included. Results it cites from other work are excluded. Hyperparameter and training choices are not treated as findings; detailed figure curves without a textual interpretation are not assigned numerical values.
record.test_reason: The study argues, and shows in a linear PCA/GAN experiment, that generative models trained by minimising a metric or f-divergence have constant test error once they interpolate, so no second descent. This is a specific challenge to the general double-descent curve (V4) for a new model class. It also reports a latent-dimension sweep of an unmodified WGAN-GP baseline. The double and triple descent it reports comes from pseudo-supervised objectives the authors built to obtain beneficial double descent, so those results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors prove and show that metric- or f-divergence-trained generative models have constant test error across interpolating solutions, so no double descent. Their best linear solution is underparameterized at k≈m. Pseudo-supervision yields beneficial double (sometimes triple) descent in linear GANs and double descent in a full-batch nonlinear WGAN-GP, with faster training. The record omits that this double descent disappears under SGD.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines GAN generation rather than the original supervised settings, varies latent dimension as a parameterization proxy, and uses 2-Wasserstein distance, geometry score, or FID. It also introduces pseudo-supervised objectives and compares distinct loss formulations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior changes with the training objective: metric minimization, pseudo-supervision, regularized pseudo-supervision, loss-term weighting, and use of a pseudo-inverse yield different curves. The nonlinear results also vary with dataset and training epoch.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding true supervised latent-output pairs to a linear generator produces a test-error peak at k=n.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Supervision reintroduces model-wise double descent in linear generative models.

fits_no_version.finding: Pseudo-supervised objectives give double descent (Eq. 4, Eq. 6 with α=0.98, and nonlinear WGAN-GP at epoch 3000) and triple descent with peaks at k=n and k=d (Eq. 7). The regularized objective (Eq. 5) does not interpolate and shows no double descent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pseudo-supervision with fabricated latent vectors can induce double or triple descent in GAN test error over latent dimension, and the effect depends on the weighting of the loss terms.

fits_no_version.finding: With SGD on full MNIST, the pseudo-supervised WGAN-GP loses double descent but still beats the baseline (Appendix E.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induced GAN double descent depends on full-batch gradient descent.

record.problems: The nonlinear experiments use MNIST and CelebA subsets and vary latent dimensionality rather than network width, depth, or parameter count. Much of the reported double or triple descent is induced by pseudo-supervision. Numerical values are often presented in plots rather than stated in text, and the nonlinear results use geometry score or FID rather than a common test-error measure.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-condition curve values and additional repeated plots are not separately extracted where the text gives only figure-level curves without a distinct textual result; see Appendix D, Figures 8–12, and Appendix E, Figures 5–7 and 13–15.

untested.parts: Model size is varied only through latent dimension k, never network width, depth or total parameter count. The interpolation threshold of the nonlinear GAN is not located.
No epoch-wise fall-rise-fall curve is clearly reported for the unmodified GANs. The training-time descriptions in R3 and R4 cannot show it.
No sweep of the number of training samples.
No label-noise sweep. No optimally tuned regularization on a naturally occurring peak. Multiple peaks appear only under the purpose-built Eq. 7 objective.
Complexity is not recounted with an effective number of parameters.

missing.what: CelebA latent-dimension sweeps at epochs 10k, 25k and 100k (baseline vs pseudo-supervised, FID); no second descent is described for the baseline.
SGD full-MNIST experiment: pseudo-supervised model loses double descent.
Theoretical Corollary 1: no double descent for any generative model minimising a metric or f-divergence.

record.verdict_notes: Parameterization is varied only by latent dimension. Nonlinear test error is geometry score (MNIST) or FID on 128 images (CelebA). Most curves are given in figures without numbers. The record conflated a dip over k with an epoch-wise dip in R3.

versions.untested_parts: It varies latent dimensionality as a proxy for parameterization, not the networks' width, depth, or total parameter count. The nonlinear GAN experiments do not establish a size at which the model just fits the training set.
The paper reports qualitative training-time behavior for GANs, but does not establish a fall-rise-fall curve across all models, latent dimensions, or datasets.
The study does not sweep the number of training samples near an interpolation threshold to test whether more data raises test error.
The study concerns GANs and PCA-related linear models, not a broad survey of model classes. Its double-descent results under pseudo-supervision are deliberately induced.
The study does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
It does not sweep label noise or establish that noise causes the peak; its regularized comparison is not described as optimally tuned.
The study does not recount complexity using an effective parameter measure to determine whether the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: linear GAN (PCA solution)
rows.size_stated: latent dimensionality k; Figure 1 does not state a numerical n
rows.operation_detail: Sweep latent dimensionality and measure test error with the 2-Wasserstein metric.
rows.value: The error has a U-shape with a minimum near k=m, then is constant for interpolating solutions when k>n.
rows.note: The authors explicitly distinguish this constant overparameterized regime from double descent.
rows.check: This is a linear PCA/LQG generator, not a deep network, so it does not bear on V1. Test error is U-shaped up to k≈m, then constant for k>n, backed by Observation 1 and Corollary 1.

rows.subject: WGAN-GP baseline

relationships.condition: Generative models trained to minimise a metric or f-divergence (linear PCA/LQG GAN; unmodified MNIST WGAN-GP at epoch 948)
relationships.reason: Linear generator test error is constant for all interpolating k>n, with no second descent, and this is proven for any metric or f-divergence objective (R1). The WGAN-GP baseline shows a dip then high error over k (R2).
relationships.display_finding: Linear-generator test error was constant for all interpolating k > n under metric or f-divergence objectives; baseline WGAN-GP showed a dip followed by high error.

relation.reason: The study supplies its own theoretical and experimental results on whether double descent occurs.

tranche.reason: Observation 1, Corollary 1 and the linear experiment specifically argue against renewed descent among exactly interpolating metric- or f-divergence-minimizing generative solutions.

source_check.notes: The constant-error theorem concerns exact interpolation of a fixed distribution under the specified distribution loss. Nonlinear double descent is reported with pseudo-supervision and full-batch training; Appendix E.1 reports its loss under SGD on the full MNIST dataset.

statements.correction: MNIST WGAN-GP; latent-dimension sweep; epoch 948; geometry score initially dips then remains high; later training reduces baseline error; nonlinear interpolation threshold not established.
statements.problem: The checkpoint-specific description is correct, but classifying this study as challenging V1 exceeds the nonlinear experiment's evidence: its interpolation threshold is not established.
